title: Threaded microfeatures — sketched PRD & stories
body:
Goal: sketch a super-lightweight feature scaffolding that lets product teams compose small, per-thread response behaviors without heavy platform changes.

Why: teams building assistants want configurable, local thread-level behavior (e.g., short summary, low-fidelity quick reply, safety hardening for finance threads) that doesn't require creating full new endpoints or model variants. We need a low-friction UX + runtime contract that can be adopted quickly and iterated on.

Non-goals: not building a new orchestration plane or replacing rollout system, not a long-term replacement for A/B rollouts. This is a user-facing composition layer that maps to existing routing/fallback primitives.

Principles:
- Minimal surface area: tiny JSON rule per thread stored in session metadata.
- Fail-safe: if rule invalid, ignore and fall back to standard route.
- Observable: log which microfeatures triggered and token delta.
- Cheap to compute: only lightweight transforms or hints to model + routing.

Core concepts (brainstorm fragments):
1) Threadlet: an opaque dict attached to a session/thread with a name, priority, and a small set of instructions.
Example: {name: "low_fidelity", priority: 50, hint: "short", max_tokens: 60, preferred_model: "opt-6b-compact"}  <-- (implementation note: we will translate to routing hint + prompt template)
2) Trigger conditions: explicit user selection, route metadata (e.g., user tier), activity type (system message), or an upstream signal (NLP classifier).
3) Handlers: inference hint (prompt modifier), routing override (prefer cheaper model), post-filter (strip sensitive PII), quick summary template.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want to toggle a thread to "concise" so that the assistant responds in 2-3 sentences for mobile users.
  Acceptance: toggle stored on thread metadata, requests include hint, responses are <80 tokens 80% of the time, telemetry shows trigger.

- As an SRE, I want lower-cost threads to be routed to compact quantized variants when load high, with fallback to baseline model on error.
  Acceptance: routing layer respects preferred_model if capacity available, logs fallback events, no user-facing errors.

- As a compliance owner, I want finance threads to always pass through a post-filter to redact account numbers before being returned.
  Acceptance: post-filter runs, any detected PANs are replaced with [REDACTED], alerts generated if filter flags anything ambiguous.

Edge cases / constraints (notes):
- Threadlets should not be able to override authorization or expose private keys. Platform ignores keys in threadlet.
- Interaction with caching: hints that change prompt shape should generally bypass prefix cache unless explicitly marked cacheable.
- Batching: small hints should be ignored for batching window selection — i.e., batching must be preserved where it matters to throughput.

Telemetry & metrics to track (initial):
- % of requests with active threadlets
- token delta (baseline vs actual) for low_fidelity threadlets
- routing fallbacks triggered due to preferred_model unavailability
- post-filter redaction counts and false positive signals (manual review sample)

Quick rollout sketch:
Phase 0: behind dev flag, only in playground + internal mobile build, simple hint->prompt transform, no routing override (safe). Metrics only.
Phase 1: allow preferred_model hint for non-Sensitive cohorts, enable routing override with explicit guardrails (capacity check + fallback). Beta customers opt-in.
Phase 2: post-filter handlers enabled, expose admin UI in console for threadlet templates and experimentation.

Simple prompt transform examples (dev note):
- concise: prepend system instruction: "Answer concisely in 2 sentences. Prioritize brevity."
- summary-short: after user message, run a summarization step before main response, use summary as context.
- quick-exec: prefer single-shot completion, max_tokens 80, stop early on newline.

Open questions / TODOs (fragments):
- storage: persisted on session store? local per-request? probably session DB with TTL to avoid long-term cruft. (ASK: SRE on costs)
- API shape: should we expose a thin /v1/threadlets endpoint, or piggyback on existing session update? Prefer piggyback initially.
- security review for post-filter handlers (what runs where).
- conflicts: multiple threadlets on same thread with different priorities — need deterministic merge (highest priority wins, otherwise merge hints with strict rules).

Low-fi mockup (console admin):
[Console] -> Threadlet templates -> New -> Name: "concise-mobile" -> Handler: prompt_transform -> default max_tokens 80 -> Allowed tiers: free, pro -> Save
Instrument: template_id on session metadata.

Acceptance testing ideas:
- Perf: smoke tests that threadlet toggles do not increase P95 latency by >10ms on median short queries.
- Correctness: golden prompt snapshots with threadlet on/off to validate prompt changes.
- E2E: integrate with routing sim to ensure preferred_model hint applied when capacity available.

Implementation sketch for infra folks (notes to self):
- request pipeline: receive request -> attach session metadata -> evaluate triggers -> expand threadlet into runtime hints -> routing decision -> prompt transform -> inference -> post-filter -> respond.
- minimal proto change: add optional field "thread_hints" to inference request protobuf (map<string,string>) so that runtime doesn't need heavy parsing. Keep schema flat.

Potential risks:
- explosion of variants if teams paper over real product needs by creating many threadlets; mitigate with quotas and template library.
- observability overhead if we log too verbosely; sample logs by default.

Notes to self: ping @mika in #prod-hosted-api about preferred_model guardrails, ask @noah about session TTL costs, link to RED-4321 for routing sim baseline.

Next actions (week):
- write short tech note for infra (~1 page) describing request lifecycle change (deadline Feb 19)
- prototype prompt_transform for concise + test readability with internal users (Feb 22)
- add simple telemetry events and dashboards (Feb 28)

Random brainlets:
- Could we implement a "micro A/B" where a threadlet exposes a boolean experiment flag that flips a single handler between two templates? Low-friction product experiments.
- Consider allowing per-thread cooldowns to avoid frequent toggles (e.g., user toggles concise on/off repeatedly).

This doc intentionally rough — notes, TODOs, and questions are here as memory. Will refine after quick sync with infra and SDK owners.

References: slack thread #prod-hosted-api: "threadlets idea" (Feb 3), GH PR above (proto change draft), RED-4321 routing sim ticket.

-- Petra
